Orto Botanico di Padova is a themed comparison candidate: Padua's Orto Botanico was founded in 1545 and survives as a named, maintained public botanical garden at its historic site.

Orto botanico di Pisa is a themed comparison candidate: Pisa's botanical garden was founded in 1544 and moved within Pisa before settling at its present site in the sixteenth century, where it remains public.
Orto Botanico di Palermo is a themed comparison candidate: Palermo's Orto Botanico was established in 1789 and remains a large, named, maintained botanical garden open to ordinary visitors.

Orto Botanico dell'Università di Catania is a themed comparison candidate: Catania's university botanical garden was founded in 1858 and continues as a distinct urban garden available for public visits.
Orto Botanico di Roma is a themed comparison candidate: Rome's current Orto Botanico was established at the Villa Corsini site in 1883 and remains a maintained public botanical garden.
Orto Botanico di Firenze is a themed comparison candidate: Florence's Orto Botanico, also called the Giardino dei Semplici, was founded in 1545 and remains a visitable maintained garden.
Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid is a themed comparison candidate: Madrid's Royal Botanical Garden was founded in 1755 and moved to its current Paseo del Prado site in 1781, where it remains public.
Jardim Botânico da Ajuda is a themed comparison candidate: Ajuda Botanical Garden was established in 1768 and remains a distinct maintained botanical garden with public access in Lisbon.

Jardim Botânico da Universidade de Coimbra is a themed comparison candidate: The Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra was founded in 1772 and remains a maintained, publicly visitable garden within Coimbra.

University of Copenhagen Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: Copenhagen's botanical garden traces its institution to 1600 and has occupied its current garden site since 1874, remaining publicly accessible.

University of Oslo Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: The University of Oslo Botanical Garden was founded in 1814 at Tøyen and remains a maintained public botanical garden in the city.

University of Tartu Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: The University of Tartu Botanical Garden was founded in 1803 and continues as a maintained, publicly visitable garden within Tartu.

Dimitrie Brândză Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: Bucharest's Dimitrie Brândză Botanical Garden was founded in 1891 and remains an individually named maintained botanical garden open to visitors.

Botanical Garden of the Komarov Botanical Institute is a themed comparison candidate: The botanical garden on Saint Petersburg's Aptekarsky Island descends from the Apothecary Garden founded in 1714 and remains a visitable maintained garden.

O.V. Fomin Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: Kyiv's O.V. Fomin Botanical Garden was established in 1839 and remains a distinct maintained botanical garden with regular visitor access.

Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden is the round target: The Indian Botanic Garden at Shibpur was established in 1787 and remains a maintained, ticketed botanical garden within the Howrah urban municipality.
Lalbagh Botanical Garden is a themed comparison candidate: Lalbagh Botanical Garden was begun in 1760 and remains a large, officially named and maintained public botanical garden in Bengaluru.

theme.title: Pre-1900 Botanical Gardens in Cities
theme.introduction: A location qualifies only if it is a distinct, officially named botanical garden or botanic garden inside a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality. The garden must have been established or opened at its current site no later than 31 December 1899, still physically exist as a garden, and offer regular public visitation. Plausible locations include: Oxford Botanic Garden (Oxford); Cambridge University Botanic Garden (Cambridge); Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (London); Chelsea Physic Garden (London); Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh (Edinburgh); Belfast Botanic Gardens (Belfast); National Botanic Gardens of Ireland, Glasnevin (Dublin); Hortus Botanicus Leiden (Leiden); Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam (Amsterdam); University Botanic Gardens Utrecht (Utrecht); Orto botanico di Padova (Padua); Orto botanico di Pisa (Pisa); Orto botanico dell’Università di Bologna (Bologna); Orto Botanico di Palermo (Palermo); Orto Botanico di Roma (Rome); Orto Botanico di Catania (Catania); Royal Botanic Garden of Madrid (Madrid); Jardim Botânico da Ajuda (Lisbon); Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra (Coimbra); Copenhagen Botanical Garden (Copenhagen); Jardin des Plantes (Paris); Saint Petersburg Botanical Garden (Saint Petersburg); Tbilisi Botanical Garden (Tbilisi); New York Botanical Garden (New York City); Missouri Botanical Garden (St. Louis); Atlanta Botanical Garden (Atlanta); Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden (Rio de Janeiro); Buenos Aires Botanical Garden (Buenos Aires); Lalbagh Botanical Garden (Bengaluru); Government Botanical Garden (Ooty); Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (Howrah/Kolkata); Peradeniya Royal Botanic Gardens (Kandy); Hong Kong Zoological and Botanical Gardens (Hong Kong); Koishikawa Korakuen Botanical Garden (Tokyo); Melbourne Royal Botanic Gardens (Melbourne); Adelaide Botanic Garden (Adelaide); Brisbane City Botanic Gardens (Brisbane); Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens (Hobart); Wellington Botanic Garden (Wellington); Durban Botanic Gardens (Durban); and Bogor Botanical Gardens (Bogor).
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when all conditions are met: (1) it is an individually named institution whose official name or governing authority identifies it as a botanical garden, botanic garden, or equivalent historical botanical-garden institution; (2) the garden was established or opened at the same identifiable site on or before 31 December 1899; (3) the historic garden still physically exists as a maintained garden; (4) it is regularly open to ordinary visitors, whether free or ticketed; (5) the garden lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) the exact garden can be pinned as a single visitable location rather than an entire metropolitan region.
